name: BICEP2 I: Detection Of B-mode Polarization at Degree Angular Scales
notes: The paper's own title says "Detection of B-mode Polarization". The Atlas result type `anomaly` records that the excess was later attributed largely to dust, per the joint BICEP2/Keck/Planck paper cited in `why_it_matters`.

summary.plain: BICEP2 reported in March 2014 an excess of B-mode polarization at degree scales that, if primordial, would have been a signature of gravitational waves from inflation. A joint analysis with Planck data in 2015 found the excess consistent with galactic dust.
summary.technical: BICEP2 I: 3 seasons, 380 deg^2, 87 nK deg depth; B-mode excess at 30 < l < 150 > 5 sigma over lensed-LCDM; r = 0.20 (+0.07/-0.05) with r = 0 disfavored at 7.0 sigma before dust correction; the abstract itself warned that dust models could not exclude explaining the entire excess.

title: BICEP2 I: Detection Of B-mode Polarization at Degree Angular Scales
why_it_matters: The abstract says "Accounting for the contribution of foreground dust will shift this value downward"; the 2015 BICEP2/Keck/Planck joint analysis found "strong evidence for dust and no statistically significant evidence for tensor modes" (arXiv:1502.00612). Recorded as an anomaly because the signal was reported as a detection but was not confirmed as primordial.
